newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori in helicopter flight scare.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori in helicopter flight scare.

text.p: A helicopter carrying Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori was declared in a state of emergency for several minutes as a technical fault caused pilots to briefly lose control of the aircraft, officials said on Sunday.

New Presidency Minister Daniel Hokama and Justice Minister Carlos Hermoza Moya were also on board the helicopter on Saturday, when the cockpit filled with smoke and forced the pilot to steer the craft with his head leaning out of the window.
"The emergency lasted a few minutes, but the president stayed calm and the flight continued normally," a palace official said.
The helicopter's co-pilot needed stitches after a blow to the head, but none of the other 17 pasengers, who included journalists and cabin crew, were injured, the official said.

The incident occurred close to the city of Santa Lucia, Puno, about 815 miles (1,300 km) southeast of Lima, on one of the many flights Fujimori takes as he makes almost daily visits to communities in Peru's interior.
